Yes, switch to Claude Desktop. But running inside Orca isn't really the problem. The bigger issue is that this session runs in the old WSL copy of the repo.

**Why running inside Orca is fine**
- Orca normally keeps its terminals in a separate background process. Quitting, restarting or updating Orca leaves that process running, so a Claude session survives and reconnects. I checked this in Orca's source. The one thing that does end your terminals is Settings → Terminal → Manage Sessions → Restart daemon.
- Our plugin runs in its own process with timeouts, so a broken plugin can't take your terminals down.

**What's actually wrong with this session**
- It runs in `~/orca-entire-extension`, the old WSL copy. Entire records this chat against that repo, not the Windows one where the code now lives.
- Every test and every `entire` or `orca` command has to cross from WSL into Windows, and Orca's WSL settings leak into those Windows programs. For example, the Windows `entire status` I ran from here picked up this session's Linux Claude config path and rejected it.

**For the new session**
- In Claude Desktop, start a **Local** session (not WSL) on `C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension`. You have Desktop 4.29 installed, plus Claude Code 2.1.311 on Windows if you'd rather use a terminal.
- Desktop reads the same settings files as the CLI, so the repo's Entire hooks should work. To confirm, run `entire status` after your first prompt and check that it lists the session. If Desktop was already open when you installed the Entire nightly, restart it so it picks up the new PATH.
- With Claude outside Orca, you can also restart Orca's terminal daemon, upgrade Orca, or run a test build of Orca without affecting Claude.
- Staying in Orca would also work, if you open a workspace on the Windows repo (it's already registered in Orca). Either way, stop using this WSL session.

**What I added so the new session has the context**
A Windows session won't see my memory or this chat, so I put what it needs into the repo:
- **`CLAUDE.md`** points to `docs/PLAN.md` and lists the commands, gotchas and rules. The rules: Entire setup commands are yours to run, Claude asks before writing anything to Entire, and trail text is treated as untrusted.
- **The test harness** was in my temporary folder and would have disappeared with this session. It's now in `scripts/orca-harness/`. It runs the plugin inside `Orca.exe` the way Orca does, without the UI: `node scripts/orca-harness/launch.mjs no-terminal`.
- **Docs:** I updated the README, and `docs/PLAN.md` now says Windows runs the Entire nightly.
- **Checked:** all 9 tests pass and the harness worked in every scenario. Pointed at this session's own Orca terminal, it reached the WSL Entire nightly (205 ms) and found the repo enabled. It found no trail on `main`, as expected.

**Your setup is good.** The Entire nightly and `git-remote-entire` are on the Windows PATH, and no older copy gets in the way. Claude Code's hooks are up to date. Codex's hooks in this repo are out of date, which only matters if you use Codex here. The fix is `entire agent add codex`. It rewrites the committed `.codex/hooks.json`, so run it on a branch.

**Before you close this session**
- Nothing is committed. Have the new session commit on a branch, so the Entire checkpoint ends up in the Windows repo with the code.
- This planning chat would only become an Entire checkpoint through a commit in the WSL copy. If you don't need it on record there, you can delete that copy. The raw chat log stays in `~/.claude` either way.

Suggested first prompt for the new session: *"Read CLAUDE.md and docs/PLAN.md. We're at the phase 0.5 smoke test."*
</pasted_content id="a49e">

1	# Entire for Orca: plan
2	
3	Bring Entire (trails, findings, approvals, checkpoints) into Orca's UI as an Orca plugin, the way
4	Orca already surfaces GitHub pull requests and checks.
5	
6	Status: phase 0 done. Next: the smoke test, then phase 1 spikes.
7	
8	## Environment
9	
10	- Orca desktop runs on Windows (1.4.245). Plugins are in alpha: manifest format 2, host API 1.0.
11	- Most Orca and Entire projects live in WSL (`\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\...`). Orca also has an SSH host.
12	- Entire CLI `0.12.3-nightly` on both sides: WSL (keyring login) and Windows in `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`
13	  (Credential Manager login).
14	- This repo: `C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension`, origin
15	  `entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/et/entire-repos/orca-entire-extension`, Entire enabled.
16	
17	## What Orca's plugin API allows today (1.4.245)
18	
19	Sources: `docs/reference/plugin-*.md` and `src/shared/plugins/**` in github.com/stablyai/orca.
20	
21	- `execution: "trusted-worker"`: `main` runs in a Node process Orca forks on the desktop host (Windows
22	  here). It has full Node access, but its env is an allowlist (PATH, HOME, USERPROFILE, TEMP and a few
23	  Windows system variables; no APPDATA). Idle workers stop after 5 minutes with nothing in flight, and a
24	  command must answer within 30 seconds.
25	- Host API 1.0: `workspace.readContext` returns `{ branch, displayName, terminals: [{ id }] }` with no
26	  path; `notifications.show`; `terminal.sendText` (worker only); `storage.*`, `secrets.*` and
27	  `settings.*` (worker only).
28	- Events (at most 3): `workspace.created`, `workspace.removed`, `agent.status.changed`.
29	- Panels are sealed: Orca injects CSP `connect-src 'none'`, blocks links and `window.open`, and gives a
30	  panel no channel to its own worker. A panel cannot show Entire data yet.
31	- Reserved but not shipped: `taskSources`, `statusBarItems`, `sidebarCards`, `connections`, `settings`,
32	  `hooks`, `skills`, `mcpServers`.
33	- The installed build has no `orca plugin ...` CLI (it is on Orca's `main`). Load the plugin through
34	  Settings → Plugins → Development folders.
35	- On 1.4.245 the manifest must keep `publisher` (leaving it out needs `>=1.4.246`). When distributing,
36	  it must equal the GitHub owner of the repository Orca installs from. Ids may not start with `orca-`.
37	
38	## Spike results (2026-10-30)
39	
40	Run from Windows Node with the worker's env allowlist:
41	
42	- `wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -e bash -lc 'exec entire "$@"' entire trail list ... --json` works with the WSL
43	  login, in 0.6–0.8 s per call.
44	- Orca's CLI (`resources\bin\orca.exe` beside the app) works once APPDATA is derived from USERPROFILE.
45	  `worktree list` takes about 2.1 s.
46	- `readContext` terminal ids are Orca CLI terminal handles. `orca terminal show --terminal <id> --json`
47	  returns the workspace's `worktreePath` (e.g. `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\peterc\ccw`), which gives the
48	  distro and Linux path.
49	- Entire has `--json` on `status`, `trail list/show/approvals/finding`, and `trail watch --json`
50	  (the trail's SSE stream as JSON lines). `trail show` exits 1 when the branch has no trail.
51	
52	## Architecture
53	
54	- One `trusted-worker` plugin. The worker is the only part that talks to Entire.
55	- Find the focused workspace's path: first terminal handle from `readContext` → `orca terminal show`.
56	  Fallback: match branch and name against `orca worktree list`. This is a stopgap until `readContext`
57	  carries a path (see the asks below).
58	- Run Entire where the repo and its login live. For a WSL path, use
59	  `wsl.exe -d <distro> --cd <path> -e bash -lc 'exec entire "$@"' entire ...`. For a local path, run
60	  `entire` directly. SSH workspaces come later.
61	- Shell out to the Entire CLI rather than calling its REST API. The CLI owns login, contexts and cell
62	  routing, so the plugin never holds a token. `entire api` covers gaps.
63	- Cache per repo and branch, refresh on `agent.status.changed`, and tail `trail watch --json` while the
64	  worker is alive.
65	- Panels only render what worker commands return. Feature-detect with `orca.host.has(...)` so one build
66	  runs on shipped and newer Orca.
67	- Entire text (intent, findings, comments) is untrusted: render it as text and never execute it.
68	
69	## GitHub feature → Entire equivalent
70	
71	| Orca + GitHub today             | Entire equivalent                                  | Unblocked by                     |
72	| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
73	| PR and CI notifications         | trail events → notifications                       | shipped API                      |
74	| Create, approve, merge a PR     | `trail create`, `approve`, `merge` as commands     | shipped API                      |
75	| Checks sidebar, review comments | trail panel: gates, CI runs, findings, approvals   | Orca #25256                      |
76	| Issues on Tasks → new workspace | trails tab → start a workspace on the change       | Orca #26282                      |
77	| PR badge on the workspace card  | trail badge on the card                            | #26282, then a forge provider    |
78	
79	For `et/` repos (`entire://` remotes, like this one) Orca has no forge integration at all, so this
80	plugin is the only one. For GitHub repos it sits beside Orca's GitHub support.
81	
82	## Phases
83	
84	- [x] 0. Repo on Windows, Entire enabled in WSL and on Windows, project added to Orca.
85	- [ ] 0.5 Smoke test: load the dev plugin and run **Entire: Check connection** in a WSL workspace and in
86	      this one.
87	- [ ] 1. Spikes: real trail JSON fixtures (create a test trail), `trail watch` through `wsl.exe` versus
88	      the 5-minute reaper, the plugin consent flow, latency budget.
89	- [ ] 2. v0.1 on shipped Orca: commands (show trail, findings, approve, merge, create, refresh) and
90	      notifications when an agent finishes and on trail events.
91	- [ ] 3. Trail panel. Needs a panel → worker channel (Orca #25256).
92	- [ ] 4. Trails tab on the Tasks page and a settings form (Orca #26282).
93	- [ ] 5. Deeper: status bar item, forge provider for `entire://` remotes, Entire agent hooks and skills,
94	      checkpoints, `entire why`, `entire review`.
95	- [ ] 6. Distribution: a GitHub mirror (Orca installs over https Git and derives the publisher from the
96	      owner), then a catalog listing.
97	
98	## Asks for the Orca team
99	
100	1. A channel from a panel to its own worker (#25256, or a push channel). It blocks any live panel.
101	2. `workspace.readContext`: add the worktree id, path and host (local, WSL, SSH).
102	3. Task sources and plugin settings (#26282), with a start recipe that can check out an existing branch.
103	4. Status bar items and sidebar cards (#23143, #26951).
104	5. Opening external URLs from panels and workers (#27568).
105	6. Long-lived worker subscriptions: the 5-minute idle reaper stops `trail watch`.
106	7. A way to run a command on the workspace's host (WSL, SSH) from a worker.
107	
108	## Risks and open questions
109	
110	- Phases 3–5 depend on unmerged Orca PRs: #25256 quiet since Oct 7, #26282 active, #15315 (forge
111	  providers) stale since August.
112	- The WSL bridge does not cover SSH workspaces.
113	- WSL runs Entire 0.12.3-nightly and Windows runs 0.12.2. On Windows, `entire status` reports the Claude
114	  Code and Codex hooks as out of date. Align the versions before running `entire doctor`, since it
115	  rewrites committed hook files.
116	- A worker's PATH comes from Orca's environment at launch. Restart Orca after installing Entire on
117	  Windows.
118	- Can #26282's start recipe check out an existing branch, or only branch off a base?

7	export function run(command, args, { cwd, env = process.env, signal, timeoutMs = CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS } = {}) {
8	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
9	    const started = Date.now()
10	    const child = spawn(command, args, { cwd, env, signal, windowsHide: true })
11	    const stdout = []
12	    const stderr = []
13	    let timedOut = false
14	    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
15	      timedOut = true
16	      child.kill()
17	    }, timeoutMs)
18	    child.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => stdout.push(chunk))
19	    child.stderr.on('data', (chunk) => stderr.push(chunk))
20	    child.on('error', (error) => {
21	      clearTimeout(timer)
22	      reject(error)
23	    })
24	    child.on('close', (code) => {
25	      clearTimeout(timer)
26	      resolve({
27	        code,
28	        timedOut,
29	        stdout: Buffer.concat(stdout).toString('utf8'),
30	        stderr: Buffer.concat(stderr).toString('utf8'),
31	        ms: Date.now() - started

1	# Entire for Orca
2	
3	An Orca plugin that brings Entire trails, findings and checkpoints into Orca. The plan, the API limits
4	it works within, and the spike results are in [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md).
5	
6	## Try it
7	
8	Requires Orca 1.4.245 or later, and the Entire CLI logged in wherever your repos live (WSL or Windows).
9	
10	1. In Orca, open **Settings → Plugins** and turn plugins on.
11	2. Click **Development folders…**, add this folder, then review and enable **Entire**.
12	3. Focus a workspace and run **Entire: Check connection** from the command palette.
13	
14	Orca reloads the plugin when its manifest changes; after editing the worker, use **Restart** on the
15	plugin's row.
16	
17	## Develop
18	
19	No build step yet: the worker is plain ES modules under `src/worker`.
20	
21	```sh
22	node --test
23	```
24	
25	To run the worker inside Orca's own runtime without the GUI (Windows, Orca installed):
26	
27	```sh
28	node scripts/orca-harness/launch.mjs no-terminal
29	```

# Orca plugin host API reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm generate:plugin-schemas` from src/shared/plugins. Do not edit. -->

Host API 1.0 (`"pluginApi": 1`). Workers call a method with `await orca.host.call(name, params)`; panels and custom editors call the same methods through `window.orca.host.call(name, params)`. Each method lists the surfaces allowed to call it; any other surface gets `not_permitted`. `orca.host.has(name)` answers synchronously whether this Orca offers a method on the current surface, and `orca.api` is `{ major, minor }`. See [Plugin authoring](./plugin-authoring.md) for the frame API.

Every call is checked against the capabilities the user approved, and params are validated before Orca runs anything: params are strict, so a field this Orca does not know is refused with `invalid_params` instead of being dropped. Mutations are recorded in the audit log as `plugin:<publisher>.<id>`.

## Methods

| Method | Capability | Surfaces | Mutation | Since | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`workspace.readContext`](#workspacereadcontext) | `workspace:read` | worker, panel, editor | no | 1.0 | Branch, name and terminal ids of the focused workspace, or null when none is focused. |
| [`terminal.sendText`](#terminalsendtext) | `terminal:send` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Types text into one terminal named by id, optionally pressing Enter. |
| [`notifications.show`](#notificationsshow) | `notifications:show` | worker, panel, editor | yes | 1.0 | Shows a desktop notification. |
| [`storage.get`](#storageget) | `storage:own` | worker | no | 1.0 | Reads a JSON value from the plugin's private store; null when absent. |
| [`storage.set`](#storageset) | `storage:own` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Writes a JSON value to the plugin's private store. |
| [`storage.delete`](#storagedelete) | `storage:own` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Removes a key from the plugin's private store. |
| [`storage.keys`](#storagekeys) | `storage:own` | worker | no | 1.0 | Lists the keys in the plugin's private store. |
| [`secrets.get`](#secretsget) | `secrets:own` | worker | no | 1.0 | Reads a secret from the plugin's encrypted secrets file; null when absent. |
| [`secrets.set`](#secretsset) | `secrets:own` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Stores a secret in the plugin's encrypted secrets file. |
| [`secrets.delete`](#secretsdelete) | `secrets:own` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Removes a secret from the plugin's encrypted secrets file. |
| [`settings.get`](#settingsget) | `settings:own` | worker | no | 1.0 | Reads every setting the plugin owns. |
| [`settings.set`](#settingsset) | `settings:own` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Writes one setting the plugin owns. |

### `workspace.readContext`

Branch, name and terminal ids of the focused workspace, or null when none is focused.

```ts
(params: {}) => { branch: string; displayName: string; terminals: { id: string }[] } | null
```

### `terminal.sendText`

Types text into one terminal named by id, optionally pressing Enter.

```ts
(params: { terminalId: string; text: string; enter?: boolean }) => { accepted: boolean }
```

### `notifications.show`

Shows a desktop notification.

```ts
(params: { title: string; body?: string }) => { delivered: boolean }
```

### `storage.get`

Reads a JSON value from the plugin's private store; null when absent.

```ts
(params: { key: string }) => { value: JSON }
```

### `storage.set`

Writes a JSON value to the plugin's private store.

```ts
(params: { key: string; value: JSON }) => { ok: true }
```

### `storage.delete`

Removes a key from the plugin's private store.

```ts
(params: { key: string }) => { ok: true }
```

### `storage.keys`

const subscription = orca.on('theme', ({ colorScheme }) => {})
subscription.dispose()
```

Methods, their surfaces and their errors are in the [host API reference](plugin-host-api.md).
Aborting the `signal` rejects the call with `cancelled`. Treat an error `code` you do not know as
`action_failed`. Params are strict: a field the running Orca does not know is refused with
`invalid_params`, so check `orca.host.has` or `orca.api.minor` before using a newer one.

Workers get the same calls on the `orca` object passed to `activate(orca)`:
`orca.api`, `orca.host.call(method, params, { signal })`, `orca.host.has(method)`, plus
`orca.commands.register(id, (args, { signal }) => …)` and `orca.events.on(event, handler)`, which
both return `{ dispose() }`. A command's `signal` aborts when Orca stops waiting for it. In
`agent.status.changed`, `state` and `mainAgent.state` are one of `working`, `blocked`, `waiting`
and `done`.

### Custom editors

A custom editor opens files that end in one of its `extensions` (with the dot, such as
`.excalidraw`) or carry one of its exact `filenames` in the editor tab, beside Source. Syntaxes
match files the same way. It runs in the same sandboxed frame as a panel (no Node, no file system), and Orca keeps
the buffer, dirty state, saving, the external-change banner, read-only tabs and remote (SSH or
paired host) files; the frame only gets the document, never a path. Editor and panel plugins are
trusted code, and an editor can read every file it opens, so install ones you trust.

An editor's `window.orca` adds `document`:

```js
const doc = await orca.document.get() // { version, readOnly, content, fileType? }
// The current document right away, then each one Orca sends when the file changes outside the editor.
orca.document.onDidChange((doc) => render(doc))
await orca.document.applyEdit({ baseVersion: doc.version, content: { kind: 'text', text } })
orca.on('editor.flush', () => sendPendingEdit()) // before a save; Orca waits for the promise
```

`content` is `{ kind: 'text', text }` for a text editor (the default `contentKind`). An edit is
the full new content, made against document `baseVersion`; send one only when the user changes
the document, never on load. `applyEdit` rejects with `conflict` when the file changed outside
the editor since that version (edit the newer document instead), `too_large` past the size cap,
and `not_permitted` when `readOnly` is true (an agent transcript, say). `version` rises with each
document Orca sends, not with your own edits.

Set `"contentKind": "bytes"` for a binary format such as a spreadsheet. Orca reads the file
itself (locally, over SSH or from a paired host) and the document's `content` is
`{ kind: 'bytes', bytes }`, where `bytes` is an `ArrayBuffer`, plus the matched suffix as
`fileType`. An edit is the whole new file the same way: `content: { kind: 'bytes', bytes }`.
Orca marks the tab dirty and saves the bytes with the tab's normal save, replacing the file
atomically; a save is refused if the file changed on disk since the document's version, and the
banner offers Reload or Overwrite. Saving to a remote host needs an Orca server new enough to
replace binary files. Source shows the binary placeholder, unsaved bytes are not kept across
restarts, and bytes tabs don't autosave.

export type PluginLogLine = { ts: number; level: 'info' | 'warn' | 'error'; line: string }

const LOG_RING_LIMIT = 200
export const PLUGIN_LOG_KEY_LIMIT = 256

export class PluginLogBuffer {
  private readonly logs = new Map<string, { token: object; lines: PluginLogLine[] }>()

  get(pluginKey: string): PluginLogLine[] {
    return this.logs.get(pluginKey)?.lines ?? []
  }

  get size(): number {
    return this.logs.size
  }

  capture(pluginKey: string): (level: PluginLogLine['level'], line: string) => void {
    const token = this.ensure(pluginKey).token
    return (level, line) => {
      if (this.logs.get(pluginKey)?.token === token) {
        this.append(pluginKey, level, line)
      }
    }
  }

  clear(pluginKey: string): void {
    this.logs.delete(pluginKey)
  }

  private ensure(pluginKey: string): { token: object; lines: PluginLogLine[] } {
    let entry = this.logs.get(pluginKey)
    if (!entry) {
      entry = { token: {}, lines: [] }
      this.logs.set(pluginKey, entry)
      while (this.logs.size > PLUGIN_LOG_KEY_LIMIT) {
        const oldest = this.logs.keys().next()
        if (oldest.done) {
          break
        }
        this.logs.delete(oldest.value)
      }
    }
    return entry
  }

  append(pluginKey: string, level: PluginLogLine['level'], line: string): void {
    const ring = this.ensure(pluginKey).lines
    ring.push({ ts: Date.now(), level, line })

content.text:
You did nothing wrong, and the command probably ran. In Orca 1.4.245, the command palette runs a plugin command and **throws away whatever it returns** ([plugin-quick-actions.ts](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/v1.4.245/src/renderer/src/components/cmd-j/plugin-quick-actions.ts)). Our worker returned its report and assumed Orca would show it. Only the **Run** button on the plugin's row in Settings → Plugins shows a result, as a toast cut off at 200 characters.

**What I changed**
- [main.mjs](src/worker/main.mjs) now reports in two places:
  - **A desktop notification:** titled "Entire: connected" or "Entire: connection problem", with the check's lines as the body.
  - **The plugin's Logs:** the full report goes to stdout, which Orca shows under the plugin's Logs in Settings → Plugins.
- The command still returns the report, for the Run button.
- [orca-plugin.json](orca-plugin.json) asks for the `notifications:show` capability. I checked it against the v2 schema at the 1.4.245 tag.
- The harness fakes the notification, and [doctor.test.mjs](test/doctor.test.mjs) covers how the notification is worded. All 11 tests pass. The harness shows "connected" for the Windows terminal and "connection problem" when there's no terminal.
- CLAUDE.md and PLAN.md now note that the palette drops results.

**To test it in Orca**
1. Open **Settings → Plugins**. Orca still has the old copy of the plugin, so press **Restart** on Entire's row, or remove and re-add the development folder if Restart doesn't pick it up.
2. Approve the new **notifications** capability when Orca asks.
3. Run **Entire: Check connection** from the palette in the Windows workspace, then in a WSL one. You should get a Windows notification each time. If one doesn't appear, look at the plugin's Logs on the same Settings page: the full report and any notification error are there.

/** The plugin system's switches, approvals and dev paths, composed into GlobalSettings. */
export type PluginSystemSettings = {
  /** Master switch for the plugin system. On by default; false means no
   *  discovery, no panels, no plugin code paths run at all. */
  pluginSystemEnabled: boolean
  /** One-shot guard for the default-on rollout: a saved false from the old
   *  default flips on once; later explicit false (e.g. policy) sticks. */
  pluginSystemDefaultedOn?: boolean
  /** Qualified plugin keys (`publisher.id`) the user disabled. Discovered
   *  plugins stay listed but are not activated. */
  disabledPlugins: string[]
  /** Consent records: qualified plugin key → capability/worker-trust fingerprint.
   *  A plugin whose current fingerprint differs is pending again, so an update
   *  crossing either trust boundary re-prompts before code runs. Absent key =
   *  never consented. */
  pluginConsents: Record<string, string>
  /** Local directories loaded as dev-mode plugins (manifest hot-reload). */
  devPluginPaths: string[]
}

type PluginSystemDefaultOnSettings = Pick<
  PluginSystemSettings,
  'pluginSystemEnabled' | 'pluginSystemDefaultedOn'
>

export function normalizePluginSystemEnabledDefaultOn(
  settings: Partial<PluginSystemDefaultOnSettings> | undefined
): Required<PluginSystemDefaultOnSettings> {
  return {
    // Pre-rollout false was the old default, not an opt-out.
    pluginSystemEnabled:

  }

**What's happening**
- Orca's settings list no development folders (`devPluginPaths: []` in its profile database, which I read from a copy).

- The copy has the old code, which returns its report to the palette, and the palette throws it away. That's why you saw nothing.
- Turning the plugin off and on or pressing refresh only restarts that same old copy. That's also why Orca never asked you to approve notifications.

**To switch to the live folder**
1. In Settings → Plugins, uninstall or remove **Entire**, so the old copy is gone.
2. Click **Development folders…**, choose **Add path**, and enter `C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension`.

content.text:
The plugin works. What's failing is Windows displaying the notification.

**What Orca's records show**
- **Audit log:** Orca's plugin audit log (`%APPDATA%\orca\plugins-data\audit.log`) has two `notifications.show` calls from `plugin:petercr.entire`, 51 seconds apart, both `ok`.
- **Result:** each title was 17 characters, the length of "Entire: connected". A failure would have been "Entire: connection problem", 26 characters. So both runs found the workspace and Entire, and the repo enabled.
- **Delivery:** Orca turns a plugin notification into an ordinary Windows notification, titled `petercr.entire: Entire: connected`. It reported `ok`, so Windows received both. Orca's notifications aren't switched off in Windows' per-app settings, so they were probably muted rather than lost.

**To find them**
- Press **Win+N**. If both notifications are listed there, Windows put them away silently. That usually means Do Not Disturb or Focus is on, or banners are off for Orca, under Settings → System → Notifications.
- In Orca, open Settings → Plugins → Entire → **Logs**. The full report from each run is there, including each step's timing.

Orca 1.4.245 offers plugins nothing else for showing results: panels can't talk to their worker yet, and there's no status bar item. That's already on our list of asks for the Orca team.

1	# Orca plugin host API reference
2	
3	<!-- Generated by `pnpm generate:plugin-schemas` from src/shared/plugins. Do not edit. -->
4	
5	Host API 1.0 (`"pluginApi": 1`). Workers call a method with `await orca.host.call(name, params)`; panels and custom editors call the same methods through `window.orca.host.call(name, params)`. Each method lists the surfaces allowed to call it; any other surface gets `not_permitted`. `orca.host.has(name)` answers synchronously whether this Orca offers a method on the current surface, and `orca.api` is `{ major, minor }`. See [Plugin authoring](./plugin-authoring.md) for the frame API.
6	
7	Every call is checked against the capabilities the user approved, and params are validated before Orca runs anything: params are strict, so a field this Orca does not know is refused with `invalid_params` instead of being dropped. Mutations are recorded in the audit log as `plugin:<publisher>.<id>`.
8	
9	## Methods
10	
11	| Method | Capability | Surfaces | Mutation | Since | Summary |
12	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
13	| [`workspace.readContext`](#workspacereadcontext) | `workspace:read` | worker, panel, editor | no | 1.0 | Branch, name and terminal ids of the focused workspace, or null when none is focused. |
14	| [`terminal.sendText`](#terminalsendtext) | `terminal:send` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Types text into one terminal named by id, optionally pressing Enter. |
15	| [`notifications.show`](#notificationsshow) | `notifications:show` | worker, panel, editor | yes | 1.0 | Shows a desktop notification. |
16	| [`storage.get`](#storageget) | `storage:own` | worker | no | 1.0 | Reads a JSON value from the plugin's private store; null when absent. |
17	| [`storage.set`](#storageset) | `storage:own` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Writes a JSON value to the plugin's private store. |
18	| [`storage.delete`](#storagedelete) | `storage:own` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Removes a key from the plugin's private store. |
19	| [`storage.keys`](#storagekeys) | `storage:own` | worker | no | 1.0 | Lists the keys in the plugin's private store. |
20	| [`secrets.get`](#secretsget) | `secrets:own` | worker | no | 1.0 | Reads a secret from the plugin's encrypted secrets file; null when absent. |
21	| [`secrets.set`](#secretsset) | `secrets:own` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Stores a secret in the plugin's encrypted secrets file. |
22	| [`secrets.delete`](#secretsdelete) | `secrets:own` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Removes a secret from the plugin's encrypted secrets file. |
23	| [`settings.get`](#settingsget) | `settings:own` | worker | no | 1.0 | Reads every setting the plugin owns. |
24	| [`settings.set`](#settingsset) | `settings:own` | worker | yes | 1.0 | Writes one setting the plugin owns. |

122	## Errors
123	
124	A failed call rejects with an `Error` carrying `code`, `message`, `retryable` and, for `rate_limited`, `retryAfterMs`. Treat a code not listed here as `action_failed`:
125	
126	- `invalid_request`: the call itself is malformed.
127	- `invalid_params`: params do not match the method, including a field this Orca does not know; the message names it.
128	- `unknown_method`: the method does not exist in this Orca.
129	- `capability_denied`: the manifest does not declare the capability.
130	- `consent_required`: the plugin is disabled or the user has not approved this version.
131	- `not_permitted`: the method or document is not available here, e.g. a worker-only method from a panel.
132	- `rate_limited`: calls arrive faster than the budget; `retryAfterMs` says when to try again.
133	- `unavailable`: the service behind the method is not running yet.
134	- `action_failed`: the method ran and failed.
135	- `cancelled`: the caller aborted the call through its `signal`.
136	- `timeout`: Orca gave up waiting.
137	- `conflict`: the call was made against a stale version, e.g. an editor edit after an outside change.
138	- `too_large`: the message is larger than Orca accepts.
139	
140	## Stability and deprecation
141	
142	Plugins are in Alpha: the manifest v2 format and catalog format are stable contracts; items listed as experimental in [Plugin authoring](./plugin-authoring.md#stability) may change.
143	
144	- **Host API 1 is frozen.** Within `pluginApi` 1, methods, params and results only grow: a new method or a new optional param arrives with a higher `Since` minor, and nothing listed here is removed, renamed or narrowed.
145	- **Deprecation.** A method to be retired is marked deprecated in this table and keeps working for the rest of the major.
146	- **New majors.** A breaking change ships as a new `pluginApi` major beside the old one. Orca refuses a manifest whose `pluginApi` names a major it does not implement, with "update Orca", instead of loading it against the wrong API.
147	- **Detect, do not assume.** Check `orca.host.has(name)` or `orca.api.minor` before calling a method newer than the oldest Orca you support; a call that slips through fails with `unknown_method`.

1	# Writing an Orca plugin
2	
3	From an empty folder to a plugin anyone can install from a catalog. The field-by-field rules
4	live in the generated references: [manifest](plugin-manifest.md), [catalog](plugin-catalog.md),
5	[host API](plugin-host-api.md), [themes](plugin-themes.md) and [theme tokens](plugin-theme-tokens.md),
6	[syntaxes](plugin-syntax.md).
7	
8	## 1. Write
9	
10	A plugin is a folder (in practice its own Git repository) with `orca-plugin.json` at the root.
11	Start from `examples/plugins/orca-gleam-syntax`, which carries the JSON Schema for editor
12	completion, or from one of:
13	
14	| Example                              | Execution        | Shows                                |
15	| ------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------------ |
16	| `examples/plugins/orca-gleam-syntax` | `data`           | A syntax, no code                    |
17	| `examples/plugins/hello-orca`        | `trusted-worker` | A panel, a worker command and events |
18	
19	Set `publisher` to the GitHub or GitLab user or organization that owns your repository (`acme`
20	for `github.com/acme/gleam-syntax`), or the official and community catalogs reject the listing.
21	When copying the Gleam example, also drop its `stablyai` publisher and `orca-` id prefix: both are
22	reserved for Orca's own plugins.
23	
24	Pick the lowest `execution` profile that covers what you contribute; it decides what the user is
25	asked to approve:
26	
27	- `data`: themes, terminal themes, icon themes, syntaxes, translations. Installs in one click.
28	- `declarative`: commands that run Orca actions, shortcuts, VM recipes. Reviewed before they
29	  are enabled.
30	- `sandboxed-ui`: panels and custom editors, in a sandboxed frame that talks to Orca only
31	  through `window.orca` (see [Frames](#frames-windoworca)) and can call only the host methods
32	  whose surfaces list `panel` or `editor`.
33	  Orca's colors reach frame CSS as `--orca-background`, `--orca-foreground`, `--orca-primary`
34	  and the rest of its panel token set, so they never collide with a frame's own variables.
35	- `trusted-worker`: `main` runs in a separate Node process and can call every host method its
36	  `capabilities` allow. There is no global switch for these full-access plugins: each one runs
37	  only after the user approves it on install. An enterprise policy to block full-access plugins
38	  may come later.
39	
40	Set `engines.orca` to the newest `Since` of any field you use, and `pluginApi` (currently `1`)
41	only when a panel or worker calls the host API.
42	
43	### Frames: `window.orca`
44	
45	Before any plugin code runs, the frame shell defines a frozen `window.orca`. It is the only
46	supported way to talk to Orca; the messages underneath are internal and change without notice.
47	
48	```js
49	orca.api // { major: 1, minor: 0 }: the host API this Orca implements
50	if (orca.host.has('workspace.readContext')) {
51	  // Synchronous: is the method offered to this surface by this Orca?
52	  const controller = new AbortController()
53	  try {
54	    const context = await orca.host.call('workspace.readContext', {}, { signal: controller.signal })
55	  } catch (error) {
56	    // error.code, error.message, error.retryable, error.retryAfterMs (rate_limited only)
57	  }
58	}
59	const subscription = orca.on('theme', ({ colorScheme }) => {})
60	subscription.dispose()
61	```
62	
63	Methods, their surfaces and their errors are in the [host API reference](plugin-host-api.md).
64	Aborting the `signal` rejects the call with `cancelled`. Treat an error `code` you do not know as
65	`action_failed`. Params are strict: a field the running Orca does not know is refused with
66	`invalid_params`, so check `orca.host.has` or `orca.api.minor` before using a newer one.
67	
68	Workers get the same calls on the `orca` object passed to `activate(orca)`:
69	`orca.api`, `orca.host.call(method, params, { signal })`, `orca.host.has(method)`, plus
70	`orca.commands.register(id, (args, { signal }) => …)` and `orca.events.on(event, handler)`, which
71	both return `{ dispose() }`. A command's `signal` aborts when Orca stops waiting for it. In
72	`agent.status.changed`, `state` and `mainAgent.state` are one of `working`, `blocked`, `waiting`
73	and `done`.
74	
75	### Custom editors
76	
77	A custom editor opens files that end in one of its `extensions` (with the dot, such as
78	`.excalidraw`) or carry one of its exact `filenames` in the editor tab, beside Source. Syntaxes
79	match files the same way. It runs in the same sandboxed frame as a panel (no Node, no file system), and Orca keeps
80	the buffer, dirty state, saving, the external-change banner, read-only tabs and remote (SSH or
81	paired host) files; the frame only gets the document, never a path. Editor and panel plugins are
82	trusted code, and an editor can read every file it opens, so install ones you trust.
83	
84	An editor's `window.orca` adds `document`:
85	
86	```js
87	const doc = await orca.document.get() // { version, readOnly, content, fileType? }
88	// The current document right away, then each one Orca sends when the file changes outside the editor.
89	orca.document.onDidChange((doc) => render(doc))
90	await orca.document.applyEdit({ baseVersion: doc.version, content: { kind: 'text', text } })
91	orca.on('editor.flush', () => sendPendingEdit()) // before a save; Orca waits for the promise
92	```
93	
94	`content` is `{ kind: 'text', text }` for a text editor (the default `contentKind`). An edit is
95	the full new content, made against document `baseVersion`; send one only when the user changes
96	the document, never on load. `applyEdit` rejects with `conflict` when the file changed outside
97	the editor since that version (edit the newer document instead), `too_large` past the size cap,
98	and `not_permitted` when `readOnly` is true (an agent transcript, say). `version` rises with each
99	document Orca sends, not with your own edits.
100	
101	Set `"contentKind": "bytes"` for a binary format such as a spreadsheet. Orca reads the file
102	itself (locally, over SSH or from a paired host) and the document's `content` is
103	`{ kind: 'bytes', bytes }`, where `bytes` is an `ArrayBuffer`, plus the matched suffix as
104	`fileType`. An edit is the whole new file the same way: `content: { kind: 'bytes', bytes }`.
105	Orca marks the tab dirty and saves the bytes with the tab's normal save, replacing the file
106	atomically; a save is refused if the file changed on disk since the document's version, and the
107	banner offers Reload or Overwrite. Saving to a remote host needs an Orca server new enough to
108	replace binary files. Source shows the binary placeholder, unsaved bytes are not kept across
109	restarts, and bytes tabs don't autosave.
110	
111	Documents and edits are capped at 64 MiB, text or bytes, on every route (local, SSH and paired
112	hosts): a larger file shows "too large to open", and a larger edit is rejected with `too_large`.
113	Past 16 MiB the tab notes that the file may take a moment. Orca saves on its own save shortcut pressed
114	inside the frame, never on a call alone.
115	
116	Theme changes do not reload the frame: the shell updates the `--orca-*` variables and the
117	`light`/`dark` class on `<html>` in place and emits `theme`. Restyle from the variables, or
118	listen with `orca.on('theme', …)`, to follow it.
119	
120	## 2. Load it while you work
121	
122	1. Settings → Plugins: click **Turn on plugins**.
123	2. **Development folders…** → add the plugin folder. A development folder overrides an installed
124	   copy with the same `<publisher>.<id>`.
125	3. Review and enable it. Nothing runs before that.
126	
127	Orca watches development folders and reloads the plugin when its manifest or files change.
128	Theme, syntax and translation edits show up as you save. Panels and workers are not bound to
129	their files in development, so saving does not ask for approval again; adding a capability or
130	moving to a higher execution profile does. Shortcuts and recipes are tied to their files, so
131	each change to them is reviewed again. Use **Restart** on the plugin row after changing a
132	worker, and the plugin's logs to see what it printed.
133	
134	## 3. Validate
135	
136	```sh
137	pnpm validate:plugin path/to/plugin
138	```
139	
140	This runs the manifest checks Orca runs, strictly: unknown keys, limits, contributions beyond the
141	execution profile, and an `engines.orca` too low for the fields used. On a catalog it also
142	checks that listed images exist and fit. In a Git repository it warns when `publisher` is not the
143	owner of the `origin` remote. Run it in CI for the plugin and catalog repositories.
144	
145	## 4. Publish to a catalog
146	
147	A catalog is a Git repository with `orca-catalog.json` at its root that lists plugins and pins
148	each release to an exact commit and file hash, so Orca refuses bytes the catalog did not vouch
149	for.
150	
151	1. Commit the plugin and run `pnpm validate:plugin` on its directory. It prints the
152	   release entry for `HEAD`: version, full commit SHA, `contentHash`, execution profile, minimum
153	   Orca, contribution summary, capabilities and file types. Every field must match
154	   what Orca finds at install, so paste it rather than writing it by hand.
155	2. Add or update the plugin's entry in the catalog's `orca-catalog.json`, newest release first:
156	
157	   ```json
158	   {
159	     "id": "acme.gleam-syntax",
160	     "source": {
161	       "kind": "git",
162	       "url": "https://github.com/acme/orca-gleam-syntax.git",
163	       "ref": "main"
164	     },
165	     "categories": ["languages"],
166	     "releases": [{ "...": "the printed entry" }]
167	   }
168	   ```
169	
170	   `commit` must be a full 40-character SHA. A tag or branch name is refused by validation and
171	   skipped by Orca. Keep the previous release listed when you raise `engines.orca`, so older
172	   Orca still has something to install.
173	
174	   **One repository can hold many plugins.** Put each in its own directory, such as
175	   `plugins/gleam-syntax/orca-plugin.json`, and add `"path": "plugins/gleam-syntax"` to its
176	   `source`; validating that directory prints the `path` to use. Orca installs only that
177	   directory, and its `contentHash` covers only its files, so commits to sibling plugins never
178	   change it. Moving a plugin to another directory counts as a different repository.
179	
180	3. Run `pnpm validate:plugin path/to/catalog` and regenerate the older
181	   `orca-marketplace.json` as described in the [catalog reference](plugin-catalog.md#clients-before-format-2).
182	4. Users add the catalog under Settings → Plugins → ⋯ → **Catalog sources…** with its Git URL and ref.
183	
184	Users approve a plugin once per level of access. An update from the same repository that asks
185	for nothing new, code changes included, installs without asking again and stays enabled. Orca
186	asks again, listing what is new, when an update adds a capability, raises the execution profile,
187	adds a command, shortcut, panel or event subscription, ships virtual machine recipes, or comes from
188	a different repository.
189	
190	With **Update plugins automatically** on (the default), Orca installs such updates for enabled
191	catalog plugins by itself, checking at startup and every 6 hours. A release installs only once it
192	has been listed for 12 hours, or at once from the official catalog, so a takedown has time to land.
193	Only pinned catalog releases (a `releases` entry with its commit and content hash) install by
194	themselves; a listing without one updates only when the user clicks Update. This includes
195	full-access plugins: an update that asks for nothing new runs its new code with the access the user
196	already granted, the same way an editor's extensions update. Turn the setting off to review every
197	update. An update that needs approval is not installed: the current version keeps running and the
198	plugin shows **Update needs review**.
199	
200	## Planned contribution points
201	
202	These `contributes` keys are reserved: a manifest may list them only as empty arrays until
203	their format ships. Each is planned as declared data that Orca renders and enforces, not
204	arbitrary plugin UI:
205	
206	- `taskSources`: issue and task providers such as Asana, Linear or Jira, filled by a worker.
207	- `connections`: account providers with a host-run sign-in.
208	- `agentHarnesses`: new coding-agent harnesses described as data.
209	- `statusBarItems`: declarative status bar widgets whose values a worker updates.
210	- `sidebarCards`: declarative left-sidebar cards whose values a worker updates.
211	- `mcpServers`: MCP server definitions offered to the agents Orca launches.
212	- `skills`: agent skills shipped as files.
213	- `hooks`: agent lifecycle hooks for the agents Orca launches.
214	- `settings`: typed plugin settings shown in Orca's settings UI.
215	
216	`skills`, `mcpServers` and `hooks` will mean what they mean in agent-plugin formats such as
217	Claude Code's. Orca does not reserve `agents`, because those formats use it for subagent files.
218	
219	See [the manifest reference](plugin-manifest.md#planned-contribution-points) for details.
220	
221	## Stability
222	
223	Plugins are in Alpha: the manifest v2 format and catalog format are stable contracts; items
224	listed as experimental may change. These parts are stable and change only additively:
225	
226	- manifest format 2, capability names and execution profiles;
227	- host API 1 (`"pluginApi": 1`): method names, params, results, surfaces and error codes;
228	- the frame API `window.orca` (`api`, `host.call`, `host.has`, `on`, and `document` in custom
229	  editors) and the document `version`/`content` shape;
230	- theme token names, and theme ids once published (users' settings store them);
231	- catalog format 2 (`orca-catalog.json`).
232	
233	Experimental; these may still change without a new format:
234	
235	- the `agent.status.changed` payload: `paneKey` is not yet a terminal id `terminal.sendText`
236	  accepts;
237	- the worker process model: Node version, lifecycle and the channel to Orca. Only
238	  `activate(orca)` and `orca.api`, `orca.host`, `orca.commands`, `orca.events` and `orca.log` are
239	  promised,
240	  and workers may be stopped at any time;
241	- language-pack keys, which change when Orca's source moves or its English copy changes; packs
242	  get best-effort coverage per release;
243	- `pnpm validate:plugin` output; only its exit codes (`0` valid, `1` invalid, `2` usage) are
244	  stable;
245	- `settings:own`, which stores untyped values until plugins can declare settings;
246	- manifest format 1, which is deprecated. Catalogs need format 2.
247	
248	Data folders, `orca-plugin-image://` URLs, tab keys and the `pluginRoot` a worker receives are
249	internal.

50	export class PluginService {
51	  readonly options: PluginServiceOptions
52	  private readonly audit: PluginAuditLog
53	  private readonly workerController: PluginWorkerController
54	  private readonly contentVerifier = new PluginContentVerifier()
55	  readonly contentPacks: PluginContentPackRegistry
56	  readonly panels: PluginPanelController
57	  private readonly changeListeners = new Set<(event: PluginChangeEvent) => void>()
58	  private readonly housekeeping = new PluginServiceHousekeeping()
59	  private runtimeDelegate: PluginRuntimeDelegate | null = null
60	  private initPromise: Promise<void> | null = null
61	  private refreshChain: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve()
62	  private contentPacksReady = false
63	  private disposed = false
64	  private readonly installed = new PluginInstallationState({
65	    pluginsDir: () => getUserPluginsDir(this.options.userDataPath),
66	    deactivate: (pluginKey) => this.workerController.deactivate(pluginKey),
67	    notifyChanged: () => this.notifyChanged(false)

70	  constructor(options: PluginServiceOptions) {
71	    this.options = options
72	    this.contentPacks = new PluginContentPackRegistry(this.contentVerifier, (pluginKey) =>
73	      Boolean(this.options.getPluginKillListEntry?.(pluginKey))
74	    )
75	    this.audit = new PluginAuditLog(getPluginsDataDir(options.userDataPath))
76	    const resolveApproved = (pluginKey: string, allowRefreshPause = false) =>
77	      this.findApprovedPlugin(pluginKey, allowRefreshPause)
78	    this.panels = new PluginPanelController({
79	      resolveApprovedPlugin: resolveApproved,
80	      contentVerifier: this.contentVerifier,
81	      executeHostCall: (pluginKey, method, params, surface) =>
82	        this.executeHostCall(pluginKey, method, params, surface),
83	      log: (pluginKey) => this.installed.captureLog(pluginKey, 'error')
84	    })
85	    this.workerController = new PluginWorkerController({
86	      entryPath: options.hostEntryPath ?? '',
87	      maxActive: options.maxActiveWorkers,
88	      idleReapMs: options.idleReapMs,
89	      workerFactory: options.workerFactory,
90	      contentVerifier: this.contentVerifier,
91	      capabilities: (pluginKey) => this.getGrantedCapabilities(pluginKey),
92	      isCurrentApproved: (spec) => isApprovedWorkerSpec(spec, resolveApproved(spec.pluginKey)),
93	      isApprovalKept: (spec) => isApprovedWorkerSpec(spec, resolveApproved(spec.pluginKey, true)),
94	      executeHostCall: (pluginKey, method, params) =>
95	        this.executeHostCall(pluginKey, method, params, 'worker'),
96	      log: (pluginKey) => this.installed.logs.capture(pluginKey),
97	      onStateChanged: () => this.notifyChanged(false)
98	    })

101	  setRuntimeDelegate(delegate: PluginRuntimeDelegate | null): void {
102	    this.runtimeDelegate = delegate
103	  }
104	
105	  onChanged(listener: (event: PluginChangeEvent) => void): () => void {
106	    this.changeListeners.add(listener)
107	    return () => this.changeListeners.delete(listener)
108	  }
109	
110	  private notifyChanged(contentPacksChanged: boolean): void {
111	    for (const listener of this.changeListeners) {
112	      listener({ contentPacksChanged })
113	    }
114	  }

116	  async initialize(): Promise<void> {
117	    this.initPromise ??= this.refresh()
118	    return this.initPromise
119	  }

121	  async whenReady(): Promise<void> {
122	    await (this.initPromise ?? Promise.resolve()).catch(() => undefined)
123	    // Client reads must wait for rollback-based content validation to settle.
124	    await waitForPluginRefreshSettlement(() => this.refreshChain)
125	  }

127	  refresh(): Promise<void> {
128	    // Snapshot off→on transitions so reconciliation cannot miss worker/panel revocation.
129	    const enabled = this.options.isPluginSystemEnabled()
130	    const devPaths = this.options.getDevPluginPaths()
131	    const consentLists = snapshotPluginConsentLists(this.options)
132	    return this.enqueue(() => this.performRefresh(enabled, devPaths, consentLists))
133	  }

135	  /** Serializes discovery, removal, and reconciliation so none sees another's partial state. */
136	  private enqueue(work: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
137	    const queued = this.refreshChain.then(work)
138	    this.refreshChain = queued.catch(() => undefined)
139	    return queued
140	  }

142	  private async performRefresh(
143	    enabled: boolean,
144	    devPaths: string[],
145	    consentLists: PluginConsentLists
146	  ): Promise<void> {
147	    if (this.disposed) {
148	      return
149	    }
150	    this.contentPacksReady = false
151	    this.contentVerifier.clear()
152	    if (!enabled) {
153	      this.panels.revokeAll()
154	    }
155	    const next = enabled
156	      ? await discoverPlugins({
157	          pluginsDir: getUserPluginsDir(this.options.userDataPath),
158	          devPluginPaths: devPaths,
159	          hostVersion: this.options.hostVersion
160	        })
161	      : []
162	    if (this.disposed) {
163	      return
164	    }
165	    // Publish identity before shutdown so triggers cannot restart old code.
166	    this.installed.discovered = next
167	    await this.contentPacks.reconcile(
168	      next,
169	      (plugin) => isPluginApproved(enabled, plugin, consentLists),
170	      this.options.getKeybindings?.()
171	    )
172	    this.contentPacksReady = true
173	    const nextSpecs = collectApprovedWorkerSpecs(next, (plugin) => this.isRuntimeApproved(plugin))
174	    // Notify before slow shutdown so feature-off unmounts panels immediately.
175	    this.notifyChanged(true)
176	    await this.workerController.reconcile(nextSpecs, (key) => this.findValidPlugin(key))
177	    if (this.disposed) {
178	      return
179	    }
180	    this.housekeeping.sync({
181	      enabled,
182	      devPaths,
183	      reapIdle: () => this.workerController.reapIdle(),
184	      refresh: () => void this.refresh()
185	    })
186	    this.notifyChanged(false)
187	  }

191	  }

195	  }

197	  findValidPlugin(pluginKey: string): ValidDiscoveredPlugin | null {

201	  /** Enabled, consented and not being removed: what may open frames or hand out its files. */
202	  findApprovedPlugin(pluginKey: string, allowRefreshPause = false): ValidDiscoveredPlugin | null {
203	    const plugin = this.findValidPlugin(pluginKey)
204	    return plugin && this.canStartPluginWork(plugin, allowRefreshPause) ? plugin : null
205	  }
206	
207	  activationState(plugin: ValidDiscoveredPlugin): PluginActivationState {
208	    return livePluginActivationState(this.options, plugin)
209	  }
210	
211	  private canStartPluginWork(plugin: ValidDiscoveredPlugin, allowRefreshPause = false): boolean {
212	    return !this.installed.isRemoving(plugin) && this.isRuntimeApproved(plugin, allowRefreshPause)
213	  }
214	
215	  private isRuntimeApproved(plugin: ValidDiscoveredPlugin, allowRefreshPause = false): boolean {
216	    return (
217	      (allowRefreshPause || this.contentPacksReady) &&
218	      this.activationState(plugin) === 'approved' &&
219	      !this.contentPacks.error(plugin.pluginKey) &&
220	      !pluginPolicyBlockError(this.options, plugin.pluginKey)
221	    )
222	  }
223	
224	  workerState(pluginKey: string): { state: PluginRunState; restarts: number } {
225	    return this.workerController.state(pluginKey)
226	  }
227	
228	  activationError(pluginKey: string): string | null {
229	    return (
230	      pluginPolicyBlockError(this.options, pluginKey) ??
231	      this.contentPacks.error(pluginKey) ??
232	      this.workerController.activationError(pluginKey)
233	    )
234	  }
235	
236	  /** Null uniformly denies unapproved plugins without exposing why. */
237	  getGrantedCapabilities(pluginKey: string): PluginCapabilityKind[] | null {
238	    const plugin = this.findValidPlugin(pluginKey)
239	    return plugin && this.isRuntimeApproved(plugin)
240	      ? capabilityKinds(plugin.manifest.capabilities)
241	      : null
242	  }
243	
244	  async executeHostCall(
245	    pluginKey: string,
246	    method: string,
247	    params: unknown,
248	    surface: PluginSurface
249	  ): Promise<PluginHostCallOutcome> {
250	    return executePluginHostCallRequest({
251	      pluginKey,
252	      request: { method, params },
253	      surface,
254	      resolvePolicy: (boundPluginKey) => ({
255	        grantedCapabilities: this.getGrantedCapabilities(boundPluginKey),
256	        services: this.runtimeDelegate
257	          ? bindPluginHostServices({
258	              delegate: this.runtimeDelegate,
259	              pluginsDataDir: getPluginsDataDir(this.options.userDataPath)
260	            })
261	          : null,
262	        audit: this.audit
263	      })
264	    })
265	  }
266	
267	  async invokeCommand(pluginKey: string, commandId: string, args?: unknown): Promise<unknown> {
268	    const plugin = this.findValidPlugin(pluginKey)
269	    if (!plugin || !this.canStartPluginWork(plugin)) {
270	      throw new Error(`plugin ${pluginKey} is not enabled`)
271	    }
272	    assertPluginWorkerCommand(plugin, commandId)
273	    const handle = await this.workerController.ensure(plugin)
274	    if (!handle.commands.includes(commandId)) {
275	      throw new Error(`plugin ${pluginKey} registered no handler for ${commandId}`)
276	    }
277	    return handle.invokeCommand(commandId, args)
278	  }
279	
280	  emitEvent(event: PluginEventName, payload: unknown): void {
281	    if (!this.options.isPluginSystemEnabled() || this.disposed) {
282	      return
283	    }
284	    deliverPluginEvent({
285	      event,
286	      payload,
287	      plugins: this.installed.discovered,
288	      workerController: this.workerController,
289	      isRuntimeApproved: (plugin) => this.canStartPluginWork(plugin),
290	      grantedCapabilities: (pluginKey) => this.getGrantedCapabilities(pluginKey),
291	      logWarning: (pluginKey) => this.installed.captureLog(pluginKey, 'warn')
292	    })
293	  }
294	
295	  removePlugin(pluginKey: string, remove: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
296	    return this.enqueue(() => this.installed.remove(pluginKey, remove))
297	  }
298	
299	  async deactivatePlugin(pluginKey: string): Promise<void> {
300	    await this.workerController.deactivate(pluginKey)
301	    this.notifyChanged(false)
302	  }
303	
304	  /** Reconcile consent/enablement without rereading files or starting workers. */
305	  async reconcileActivationState(): Promise<void> {
306	    return this.enqueue(() => this.performActivationStateReconciliation())
307	  }
308	
309	  private async performActivationStateReconciliation(): Promise<void> {
310	    this.contentPacksReady = false
311	    await this.contentPacks.reconcile(
312	      this.installed.discovered,
313	      (plugin) => this.activationState(plugin) === 'approved',
314	      this.options.getKeybindings?.()
315	    )
316	    this.contentPacksReady = true
317	    const nextSpecs = collectApprovedWorkerSpecs(this.installed.discovered, (plugin) =>
318	      this.isRuntimeApproved(plugin)
319	    )
320	    await this.workerController.reconcile(nextSpecs)
321	    this.notifyChanged(true)
322	  }
323	
324	  async dispose(): Promise<void> {
325	    this.disposed = true
326	    this.housekeeping.dispose()
327	    this.panels.dispose()
328	    // Why stop workers first: a refresh may be waiting on a worker slot only shutdown releases.
329	    await Promise.all([this.workerController.dispose(), this.refreshChain.catch(() => undefined)])
330	    await this.audit.flush()
331	  }
332	}

1	import {
2	  getPluginActivationState,
3	  type PluginActivationState,
4	  type PluginConsentLists
5	} from '../../shared/plugins/approval/plugin-consent-state'
6	import type { ValidDiscoveredPlugin } from './plugin-discovery'
7	import type { PluginServiceOptions } from './plugin-service-options'
8	
9	export function snapshotPluginConsentLists(source: {
10	  getPluginConsents: () => Record<string, string>
11	  getDisabledPlugins: () => string[]
12	}): PluginConsentLists {
13	  return {
14	    pluginConsents: source.getPluginConsents(),
15	    disabledPlugins: source.getDisabledPlugins()
16	  }
17	}
18	
19	export function isPluginApproved(
20	  enabled: boolean,
21	  plugin: ValidDiscoveredPlugin,
22	  lists: PluginConsentLists
23	): boolean {
24	  return (
25	    enabled &&
26	    getPluginActivationState(plugin.pluginKey, plugin.consentFingerprint, lists) === 'approved'
27	  )
28	}
29	
30	/** The settings every plugin policy decision reads. */
31	export type PluginPolicySource = Pick<
32	  PluginServiceOptions,
33	  'isPluginSystemEnabled' | 'getPluginConsents' | 'getDisabledPlugins' | 'getPluginKillListEntry'
34	>
35	
36	/** Live consent state. The feature flag is an authority boundary, not only a discovery hint:
37	 *  callers fail closed immediately even before async reconciliation ends. */
38	export function livePluginActivationState(
39	  source: PluginPolicySource,
40	  plugin: ValidDiscoveredPlugin
41	): PluginActivationState {
42	  if (!source.isPluginSystemEnabled()) {
43	    return 'disabled'
44	  }
45	  return getPluginActivationState(
46	    plugin.pluginKey,
47	    plugin.consentFingerprint,
48	    snapshotPluginConsentLists(source)
49	  )
50	}
51	
52	/** Why the plugin may not run despite consent: Orca's safety list. Full access needs only consent. */
53	export function pluginPolicyBlockError(
54	  source: PluginPolicySource,
55	  pluginKey: string
56	): string | null {
57	  const blocked = source.getPluginKillListEntry?.(pluginKey)
58	  return blocked ? `Blocked by Orca's plugin safety list: ${blocked.reason}` : null
59	}

5	export function buildPluginWorkerSpawnSpec(
6	  plugin: ValidDiscoveredPlugin,
7	  grantedCapabilities: readonly PluginCapabilityKind[]
8	): PluginWorkerSpawnSpec {
9	  if (!plugin.manifest.main) {
10	    throw new Error(`plugin ${plugin.pluginKey} has no worker entry`)
11	  }
12	  return {
13	    pluginKey: plugin.pluginKey,
14	    rootDir: plugin.rootDir,
15	    mainEntry: plugin.manifest.main,
16	    // Dev roots survive manifest changes; include revision to prevent stale worker reuse.
17	    manifestRevision: JSON.stringify(plugin.manifest),
18	    reviewedContentHash: plugin.contentHash ?? plugin.consentContentHash ?? null,
19	    grantedCapabilities
20	  }
21	}
22	
23	export function pluginWorkerSpawnSpecsEqual(
24	  left: PluginWorkerSpawnSpec,
25	  right: PluginWorkerSpawnSpec
26	): boolean {
27	  if (
28	    left.pluginKey !== right.pluginKey ||
29	    left.rootDir !== right.rootDir ||
30	    left.mainEntry !== right.mainEntry ||
31	    left.manifestRevision !== right.manifestRevision ||
32	    (left.reviewedContentHash ?? null) !== (right.reviewedContentHash ?? null)
33	  ) {
34	    return false
35	  }
36	  const leftCapabilities = [...left.grantedCapabilities].sort()
37	  const rightCapabilities = [...right.grantedCapabilities].sort()
38	  return (
39	    leftCapabilities.length === rightCapabilities.length &&
40	    leftCapabilities.every((capability, index) => capability === rightCapabilities[index])
41	  )
42	}

5	const CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000

7	export function run(command, args, { cwd, env = process.env, signal, timeoutMs = CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS } = {}) {
8	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
9	    const started = Date.now()
10	    const child = spawn(command, args, { cwd, env, signal, windowsHide: true })
11	    const stdout = []
12	    const stderr = []
13	    let timedOut = false
14	    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
15	      timedOut = true
16	      child.kill()
17	    }, timeoutMs)
18	    child.stdout.on('data', (chunk) => stdout.push(chunk))
19	    child.stderr.on('data', (chunk) => stderr.push(chunk))
20	    child.on('error', (error) => {
21	      clearTimeout(timer)
22	      reject(error)
23	    })
24	    child.on('close', (code) => {
25	      clearTimeout(timer)
26	      resolve({
27	        code,
28	        timedOut,
29	        stdout: Buffer.concat(stdout).toString('utf8'),
30	        stderr: Buffer.concat(stderr).toString('utf8'),
31	        ms: Date.now() - started
32	      })
33	    })
34	  })
35	}

input.new_string:
- Panels are sealed: Orca injects CSP `connect-src 'none'` (scripts and styles inline only, images
  as data URLs), blocks links and `window.open`, and gives a panel no channel to its own worker. A
  panel can call only `workspace.readContext` and `notifications.show`, and loads one HTML file.
- Stopgap: Orca rereads a development folder's panel file whenever the folder changes and remounts
  the panel when the HTML differs. Writing a file there neither restarts the worker nor asks for
  approval again (only shortcuts and VM recipes tie approval to file bytes). So the worker writes its
  data into the panel file. Installed copies are hash-checked and refused once a byte changes, so
  this works only from a development folder.

content.text:
I've added an **Entire** panel to Orca's right sidebar, with a layers icon. Unit tests pass and the harness worked for a Windows and a WSL workspace, but I haven't seen it inside Orca yet, and nothing is committed.

**What the panel shows for the focused workspace**
- **Repo:** whether Entire is enabled, which agents are set up, unpushed checkpoints and the push setting, Codex hook state, and active sessions.
- **Trail:** the branch's trail, if it has one. No project here has a trail yet, so I couldn't see its real JSON. For now the panel lists the trail's plain fields as they come. Getting a real one is a phase 1 task, and creating a trail needs your OK.
- **Checkpoints:** the newest 20 on the branch, each with its message, agent, age and ID.
- **Connection:** the same check as **Entire: Check connection**.

**How the data gets in**
- The worker writes the data straight into the panel's HTML file, `panel/entire.html`. That file is generated from the committed [panel/template.html](panel/template.html) and kept out of git.
- The panel holds up to 10 workspaces and every 2 seconds checks which one is focused.
- The panel updates when you run **Entire: Refresh panel**, when you run **Check connection**, and 3 seconds after an agent finishes in Orca.
- All Entire text is treated as untrusted. It's escaped inside the HTML file and only ever displayed as text, never as markup. A test covers someone trying to break out of the data block.

**Fixed while previewing it:** a variable named `closed` in the panel script clashed with a built-in property of the browser window, and the panel would have stayed blank in Orca. I renamed it and noted the trap in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).

**To try it in Orca**
1. In Settings → Plugins, open ⋯ → **Development folders…** and add this folder. It takes over from your installed copy, which can never show data: Orca rejects an installed plugin once any of its files change.
2. Approve Entire again. Orca asks because the plugin now adds a panel, a command, an event subscription and the `agent:read` permission.
3. Focus a workspace with a terminal open and run **Entire: Refresh panel**.
4. Open the Entire panel.

`panel/entire.html` already exists in this folder. In a fresh clone, run `node scripts/create-panel.mjs` first, because Orca refuses the plugin while that file is missing.

**Code changes**
- **[src/worker/snapshot.mjs](src/worker/snapshot.mjs):** collects the data. The three Entire calls now run at the same time.
- **[src/worker/doctor.mjs](src/worker/doctor.mjs):** builds the connection report from that data.
- **[src/worker/panel.mjs](src/worker/panel.mjs):** writes the panel file, and never writes into an installed copy.
- **[src/worker/main.mjs](src/worker/main.mjs):** registers the new command and the agent event.
- **[orca-plugin.json](orca-plugin.json):** declares the panel, the command, the event and the new permission.
- **[test/panel.test.mjs](test/panel.test.mjs)** and **[test/doctor.test.mjs](test/doctor.test.mjs):** 20 tests in total now, all passing.
- **Docs:** [README.md](README.md), [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) and [docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) explain the workaround and its limits.

content.text:
The icon is missing because Orca is still running an old copy of Entire that has no panel. Orca Run isn't doing anything special.

**How Orca Run does it.** I read its installed manifest in `%APPDATA%\orca\plugins\stablyai.orca-runner\`. It declares one panel, `{ "id": "runner", "title": "Orca Run", "icon": "zap", "entry": "panel/index.html" }`, and asks for no other permissions. Its `panel/index.html` is a single file built from its `src/` by a build script. That's the same setup as ours: `"icon": "layers"` and `panel/entire.html`. Our manifest also passes Orca's v2 schema, including the `layers` icon.

**What Orca is actually running.** Orca's plugin lockfile still points Entire at the copy you installed from this folder at 5:20 PM, under `%APPDATA%\orca\plugins\petercr.entire\d515cd77…`. That copy's manifest has only the Check connection command, with no panel. Orca's settings list no development folders at all, so the new code in this repo never reaches Orca. Turning the plugin off and on, or restarting Orca, keeps loading that old copy.

**To fix it.** Load this repo as a development folder:
1. In Orca, open **Settings → Plugins**, click the **⋯** menu, then **Development folders…**.
2. Type `C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension` into the path box and click **Add path**. It's a text field, not a folder picker. A development folder replaces the installed copy, because they share the `petercr.entire` id.
3. Review and enable **Entire**. Orca asks again because the plugin now adds a panel, a command, an agent event and the `agent:read` permission.
4. The layers icon should appear next to Orca Run's ⚡. Focus a workspace with a terminal open, run **Entire: Refresh panel**, and open the panel.

Don't install it from the folder again instead. That makes another frozen copy: the icon would show, but the worker never writes into an installed copy, so the panel would never update.

content.text:
I rebuilt the panel to look like Orca's own source-control sidebar, and Checkpoints now starts closed. I also rewrote `panel/entire.html` from the new template, so Orca should already show the new look without a refresh.

**What changed in [panel/template.html](panel/template.html)**
- **Header:** the workspace name with a colored dot (green when connected, amber when Entire isn't enabled, red on a problem) and how long ago the data was refreshed. The path sits under it. The branch shows only when it differs from the workspace name.
- **Summary:** short labels in place of the old list, showing Enabled, each agent, and the number of unpushed checkpoints.
- **Warnings:** a "Codex hooks are out of date" note, and any sync error, each show as a single highlighted line.
- **Sections:** headers like Orca's "COMMITS", in small capitals with a chevron and a count on the right.
  - **Sessions:** open by default. It only appears when there are active sessions.
  - **Trail:** open by default. When there's no trail it just says "No trail for this branch."
  - **Checkpoints:** closed by default. Each one takes two lines: the message, then the agent, age and the first 8 characters of its ID. The full ID is in the tooltip.
  - **Connection:** closed by default, with **OK** or **Problem** on the header. It opens by itself when a check fails.
- **Text:** long text is cut to one line, with the full text on hover.

**One limit you'll notice:** Orca reloads the panel whenever new data arrives, which happens on a refresh or when an agent finishes. Any section you opened closes again then. A sandboxed panel has nowhere to remember that choice.

I checked it in dark and light mode, and for both the Windows and WSL workspaces. Tests still pass. While I was at it, I wrapped the panel script in a function so its names can't clash with the browser's built-in ones again, which was the cause of the earlier blank panel.

Trails weren't set up, so I created this repo's first one: **trail #1, "Entire for Orca: plugin scaffold and panel"**, linked to `plugin-scaffold`. Entire has no per-repo setting to turn on; trails are just created one per piece of work.

- **Branch:** `plugin-scaffold` is linked as change #1. It was already on origin, so nothing new was pushed, and my local checkout wasn't touched.

**Merge gates.** `entire trail show --json` now finds the trail from this branch, and it lists three gates on the current commit (`9e82da8`). All three block merging:

| Gate | State | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Approvals | failed | "No reviewers have approved this trail". It needs 1 reviewer, and approving your own trail is allowed. |
| Findings | not run | Not evaluated yet. |
| Up to date | passed | `plugin-scaffold` is ahead of `main` and 0 commits behind. |

So the trail can't merge until someone approves it with `entire trail approve`. That writes to Entire, so it's your call.

**The panel.** It will show this trail after your next **Entire: Refresh panel**, or the next time an agent finishes. The Trail section was written before we had a real trail, so it currently lists the trail's raw top-level fields, including internal IDs. content.text:
The Trail section now shows trail #1 properly, and the panel has a ↻ button. The ↻ works only while the plugin's worker is running. I've tested it in a preview and with unit tests, but not yet in Orca, and nothing is committed.

**What the Trail section shows now**
- **Header:** "TRAIL #1" with a badge. Right now it reads a red **Blocked**, because a required gate is failing.
- **Trail details:** the title, "Feature · 1 change", and two lines of the description.
- **One row per merge gate:** ✕ **Approvals**, "No reviewers have approved this trail", 0/1. ○ **Findings**, not evaluated yet. ✓ **Up to date**.
- **Also shown when present:** merge conflicts, CI check runs, and other branches linked to the trail.
- **Behind it:** a new [src/worker/trail.mjs](src/worker/trail.mjs) trims Entire's trail JSON down to these fields, dropping internal IDs and accounts. The real JSON for trail #1 is saved as [test/fixtures/trail-show.json](test/fixtures/trail-show.json) and tested against.

**How the ↻ reaches the worker**
- Clicking it shows a notification titled "Entire: refreshing the panel".
- Orca records every plugin notification in its audit log, but only as the title's length. So that title has a length no other Entire notification uses, and a test enforces it.
- The worker checks the log once a second. When it sees that entry, it refreshes, and Orca reloads the panel.

**What to expect when you click it**
- **Each click pops a Windows notification.**
- **It works only while the worker is running.** The worker starts when you run a command or an agent finishes, and stops after 5 idle minutes.
- **If no worker is running,** nothing refreshes. After 12 seconds the panel says to run **Entire: Refresh panel**.
- **It relies on Orca internals.** It depends on an internal Orca file, so an Orca update could break it.

**To try it in Orca:** no worker is running now, so you don't need to restart the plugin.
1. Run **Entire: Refresh panel** once. That starts a worker with the new code.
2. Click ↻ in the panel. Within a few seconds the time should change to "just now".

One harness-related note: my harness test run replaced the Windows workspace's panel data. If the panel says "No Entire data yet" for `plugin-scaffold`, step 1 fixes that.

content.text:
The ↻ click did reach Orca, but no plugin worker was running to pick it up, so nothing refreshed. I've changed the worker so it stays running for an hour after each refresh.

**What happened.** Orca's audit log has your click at 9:46:49 PM, with the exact entry the worker looks for, and the worker's code recognizes that line when run against the real log. But no Entire worker was running then, and **Entire: Refresh panel** hadn't run since 9:01 PM. That's when the panel file was last written, by my harness test. So the request had no listener. Orca stops an idle worker after 5 minutes, and it only starts one for a command or when an agent finishes.

**The fix.** Orca's idle timer resets whenever the worker itself calls Orca. So [src/worker/main.mjs](src/worker/main.mjs) now makes a cheap "which workspace is focused" call every 2 minutes, for an hour after the last refresh. Each refresh restarts that hour, whether it comes from ↻, a command or an agent finishing. Once anything has refreshed the panel, ↻ keeps working while you're using Orca. After an hour with no refresh, the worker stops as before. The next agent finishing or **Entire: Refresh panel** brings it back. If you click ↻ in that gap, the panel tells you after 12 seconds.

**To try it.** No worker is running now, so you don't need to toggle the plugin.
1. Run **Entire: Refresh panel** from the command palette. That starts the worker with this code.
2. Click ↻. Within a few seconds the time should go back to "just now". You'll also see the "refreshing the panel" notification each time.

Tests pass (28) and the harness still exits in about 3 seconds. Nothing is committed yet.

Upload the named checkpoints to the checkpoint sync remote now, the same way
git push would. Use it when the clone's checkpoint push policy is manual, so
git push leaves checkpoints on this machine, or to upload ahead of your next
push under automatic.

Each checkpoint is uploaded at its current version, with every earlier version
not yet uploaded. Run 'entire checkpoint list --outgoing' to see what is
waiting. <checkpoint-id>@<commit> uploads that checkpoint only while <commit>
is still its current version: if it changed since you looked, it is not sent.

--all and a bare <checkpoint-id> need a terminal. Without one, name each
checkpoint as <checkpoint-id>@<commit>, using the commit --outgoing --json
reports. With no arguments, it lists what is waiting and uploads nothing.

Examples:
  entire checkpoint push <id>
  entire checkpoint push --all
  entire checkpoint push <id>@<commit> --json

Usage:
  entire checkpoint push [<checkpoint-id>[@<commit>]...] [flags]

Flags:
      --all    Upload every waiting checkpoint (needs a terminal)
  -h, --help   help for push

content.text:
The popup windows came from Entire's usage analytics, not from our code, and the plugin now switches analytics off for its own Entire calls. In a traced refresh that now opens zero windows, where before it opened about eight. ↻ should work too, once Orca's running worker is replaced. Nothing is committed yet.

**Why the windows opened.** After every command, Entire launches a background copy of itself, `entire __send_analytics`, to report usage. Entire's source on GitHub shows that on Windows this copy runs with no console (`DETACHED_PROCESS`). Each `git` it runs therefore gets a new console, and Windows Terminal opens one window per console. A refresh makes four Entire calls, so you saw a burst of windows. This is a bug in Entire on Windows; anything that runs `entire` from a GUI app will hit it. If you'd like, I can draft an issue for `entireio/cli`.

**The fix.** [src/worker/entire-cli.mjs](src/worker/entire-cli.mjs) now runs every Entire call with `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1`, which Entire documents as its opt-out. It also forwards the variable into WSL. Both of your installed Entire builds honor it.
- This affects only the plugin's background calls. Analytics from Entire commands you run yourself are unchanged.
- I didn't touch `"telemetry": true` in [.entire/settings.json](.entire/settings.json). If you want analytics off for the whole repo, run `entire configure --telemetry=false` yourself.

**Why ↻ did nothing.** Both of your clicks, at 10:05:07 and 10:05:27, came before **Entire: Refresh panel** started the worker at 10:05:51. There was no worker yet to hear them. That worker is still running at 10:14, past the 5 minutes when Orca would normally have stopped it, so the keep-alive works. But it's running the code from before the fix, and it would still open windows on every refresh.

**To try it.**
1. Turn **Entire** off and on in Settings → Plugins, so Orca drops the old worker.
2. Run **Entire: Refresh panel**. It should open no windows.
3. Click ↻. Within a few seconds the time should change to "just now".

Tests pass (30, including two new ones for the opt-out). I also added a note to [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) so future code runs `entire` only through this path.
